subject: Mythology
title: Shango: God of Thunder
description: A 60-second lesson on Shango: God of Thunder.

hook.text: Shango was a real Yoruba king who became so powerful that after death he was worshipped as the god of thunder.

buildup.text: As king, he was fierce but just. His temper could destroy, but his judgment brought order to his kingdom.

discovery.text: After his death, lightning was said to be Shango striking down liars. His symbol is the double-headed axe.

twist.text: In the Americas, enslaved Yoruba matched Shango with Saint Barbara. He is now worshipped in Santeria worldwide.

climax.text: Shango's worship spans three continents. He is invoked in ceremonies from Lagos to Havana to Brooklyn.

punchline.text: A West African king became a god who is now worshipped on three continents.

quiz.question: What was Shango before he became the god of thunder?
options: A wandering priest who performed miracles
A real Yoruba king who was deified after death
A spirit created by Olorun at the beginning of time
